issues.span: hundreds of thousands of millions of eons
issues.evidence: Tibetan "བསྐལ་པ་བྱེ་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་འབུམ་ཕྲག་དུ་མར" names koṭi (བྱེ་བ) and niyuta (ཁྲག་ཁྲིག) separately; Sanskrit "kalpakoṭi-niyuta-śata-sahasrāṇi". The English drops niyuta.
issues.fix: many hundreds of thousands of niyutas of millions of eons

issues.evidence: Tibetan "སྔ་དྲོའི་དུས་ཀྱི་ཚེ" = at the time of morning; Sanskrit "pūrvāhṇakālasamaye" (forenoon). "Evening" would be ཕྱི་དྲོ/དགོང་མོ.
Tibetan "སྲོག་མེད་པ" is locked as "life-force" (Sanskrit nirjīva); "soul" is a different concept (ātman) and the glossary rendering was required.

issues.span: in this Dharma discourse being without self and unborn
issues.evidence: Tibetan "ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས་འདི་བདག་མེད་ཅིང་སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པ་ལ་བཟོད་པ་ཐོབ"; Sanskrit "nirātmakeṣv anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntiṃ" puts selflessness/unbornness on the dharmas. Vasubandhu (2-136) glosses "བདག་མེད་ཅིང་སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པའི་ཆོས་རྣམས་ལ", Chone (2-144) "མི་སྐྱེ་བའི་ཆོས་ལ་བཟོད་པ" relying on this discourse. The English can be read as the discourse itself being selfless and unborn.
issues.fix: in what this Dharma discourse teaches as being without self and unborn

issues.evidence: Tibetan "དཔེ་དང་ཟླ་དང་རྒྱུར་ཡང་མི་བཟོད་དོ" ends in the negation "མི་བཟོད" (Sanskrit "na kṣamate"): it does not bear comparison. The English reverses this.

issues.span: the Tathāgata does not know them
issues.evidence: Tibetan "དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་མཁྱེན་ཏོ" affirms that the Tathāgata knows them; Sanskrit "jñātās te ... tathāgatena".

issues.span: will also engage in the perception of a phenomenon
issues.evidence: Tibetan "ཆོས་སུ་འདུ་ཤེས་པ་དང༌། ཆོས་མེད་པར་ཡང་འདུ་ཤེས་མི་འཇུག" negates both perceptions with "མི་འཇུག"; Sanskrit "nāpi teṣāṃ dharmasaṃjñā pravartate / evaṃ nādharmasaṃjñā".
issues.fix: do not engage in the perception of a phenomenon

issues.evidence: Tibetan "མདོ་སྡེ་འདི་བཤད་པ་ལ" (when this sūtra is explained/taught; Sanskrit "sūtre bhāṣyamāṇe") is the condition under which they are not frightened; absent from the English.
issues.fix: Those sentient beings who are not terrified, not frightened, and do not become completely frightened when this sūtra is explained will be endowed with supreme wonder.

issues.evidence: Tibetan "མར་མེ་མཛད" (locked: Dīpaṃkara); Sanskrit "dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasya". The Buddha received nothing from Dīpaṃkara; "Śākyamuni" is the wrong referent.
The Tibetan "སེམས་བསྐྱེད་པར་བྱའོ" has an unstated agent (the bodhisattva); "they" most naturally refers back to the sentient beings just mentioned.
Tibetan "མི་གནས་པར་སྦྱིན་པ་སྦྱིན་པ" (locked "མི་གནས་པ" = without abiding); Sanskrit "apratiṣṭhito dānaṃ dadāti". The negation is dropped.
Tibetan "ཟིལ་བ" is locked as "dewdrop" (Sanskrit "avaśyāya"); no rainbow in the verse.
Tibetan "དེ་འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་པར་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་གསུངས་པ" (Sanskrit "asaṃjñaiṣā tathāgatena bhāṣitā"): the Tathāgata spoke of it as non-perception.

issues.span: should hold on to phenomena, let alone non-phenomena
issues.evidence: Tibetan "ཆོས་རྣམས་ཀྱང་སྤང་བར་བྱ་ན། ཆོས་མ་ཡིན་པ་རྣམས་ལྟ་ཅི་སྨོས" — "སྤང་" is abandon (Sanskrit "prahātavyāḥ"). The raft simile is about relinquishing.
issues.fix: should abandon even phenomena, let alone non-phenomena

issues.evidence: Tibetan "ཁྲི་དགུ་སྟོང" = nine thousand ten-thousands = ninety million (ཁྲི = 10,000), not nine million.

issues.span: and promised them rebirth in his pure land
issues.evidence: Tibetan "ཕན་གདགས་པའི་དམ་པ་ཇི་སྙེད་པས་ཕན་གདགས་པ" says only that he benefited them with the supreme benefit; nothing about promising rebirth in a pure land. Chone (2-3) and Vasubandhu (2-2) comment only on benefit and entrustment.
issues.fix: has benefited the bodhisattva great beings with the supreme benefits

issues.span: it is because there is a Dharma that can be apprehended
issues.evidence: Tibetan "ཆོས་དེ་གང་ཡང་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ" gives the reason as there being no such Dharma; Sanskrit "nāsti sa kaścid dharmo yo dharmadeśanā nāmopalabhyate".
issues.fix: it is because there is no Dharma that can be apprehended as "teaching the Dharma"

issues.span: has spoken of it as grasping
issues.evidence: Tibetan "འཛིན་པ་མེད་པར་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་གསུངས" and Sanskrit "agrāha eṣa tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ": spoken of as non-grasping. The English drops the negation.
issues.fix: has spoken of it as non-grasping

issues.evidence: Locked rendering of "བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ" is "unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening"; the English uses "perfect enlightenment".

issues.span: do designate some phenomena as destroyed or as an annihilation
issues.evidence: Tibetan "ཆོས་གང་ཡང་རྣམ་པར་བཤིག་པའམ། ཆད་པར་བཏགས་པ་མེད་དོ" ends in "མེད་དོ" (none); Sanskrit "na ... kasyacid dharmasya vināśaḥ prajñapto nocchedaḥ". The English asserts the opposite.
issues.fix: do not designate any phenomenon as destroyed or as an annihilation

issues.evidence: Tibetan "མཚན་སུམ་ཅུ་རྩ་གཉིས" (locked "thirty-two marks"); Sanskrit "dvātriṃśan mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni".
Tibetan "ཀུན་ཆུབ་པར་བྱེད་པ" is to understand fully; Chone (2-61) glosses it "དེའི་དོན་ཀུན་ཆུབ་པ་སྟེ་ཤེས་པ". "Masters" overstates it.
